title: It's like Cursor, but for Game Dev, just added: Free Local Opensource models: Gemma 4 & more
author: ajdare
selftext:
So this is WizardGenie - my AI Game Engine - it's alpha but available early access to supporters of this project - I also have a free to try web version and I appreciate any suggestions and feedback - So I just added free Local Opensource models: Gemma 4, Qwen, Granite and Nemotron - 1 Click install & setup. It also connects with GPT Codex subscriptions, supports BYOK for Opus/Gemini/Deepseek/Minimax (and more) as well as links up with your Cursor subscription if you have one.

The goal here is to build an AI-centric game development engine, instead of trying to shoehorn AI in an existing engines (which I found to be a bit clunky and crashy) but instead to start at a level of pure AI agentic coding & build up game development tools from there. [https://sorceress.games/](https://sorceress.games/)

comments.author: Gullible-Ad3912
comments.body: So. Why would I use this instead of a MCP for popular engines?

replies.author: ajdare
replies.body: Depends on your game creation goals and how much control you want over your game \~ one example: Unreal Engine is built around 3D characters, skeletal meshes - if you wanted to create Minecraft, you would not want to do it in Unreal Engine, it's not meant for Voxel games, the engine doesn't support voxels (unless adding some hacky plugins) If you wanted to make a 2D game you could do it in UE but again, it's primary game-type focus is 3D (yes you can fake 2D) - and If you want to vibe-code your game (any kind of game) you're going to be fighting against the major engines native framework - Vibe coding I find works best with a blank canvas. Building a game from the ground up has never been easier and it's exactly tuned to your game mechanics - it's total development freedom and innovation and in cases of certain types of games, it can be way faster too.

replies.author: Gullible-Ad3912
replies.body:
Well, not really.

You can integrate everything you mentioned into popular engines. It might be more or less convenient depending on the engine and the feature, but it is definitely very, very far from being just “hacky plugins.”

MCP projects for popular engines are advancing faster and faster every day. We are at the point where you can start to vibe-code a full game. You are definitely underestimating the actual capabilities.

Not to mention all the full AI-wrapper products for websites with AI-generated images.

Best of luck, but I think your best chance is to simply move on to another project. This has no value.
